words: No Black Diamond Cottonwood table carries an ACCOUNT-grain return column, so the verdict is ACCOUNT_VALUE_ONLY. Account-grain values and flows exist: silver fact_allocations (144 date partitions, newest 2026-10-13) carries Account Market Value, Cash Market Value and Cash Allocation beside AccountID and Account Number; silver fact_transactions (124 partitions, newest 2026-10-14) carries AccountID, Trade Date, Transaction Type, Market Value, External Flow, Income and Transaction Fee, and the gold builder reads four of them as per-account external flows. The seven pattern-matched columns are dollar gain or loss at position or lot grain: silver fact_unrealized (Total Gain Loss, Long-Term Gain/Loss, Short-Term Gain/Loss) and silver fact_realized (the same three on sold lots), plus the column Return Date in silver fact_transactions, which is a date. No column is a percentage, time-weighted or money-weighted return. An account return series would therefore be COMPUTED from account value and external flows; it is not carried in any table read. The silver fact_holdings table (93 partitions, newest 2026-10-13) is security-grain, so it is not a return source either.
grain_words: Account, by name: fact_allocations (account values), fact_transactions (flows; one transaction per row), fact_model_assignment (account attributes). Account and security, per day: fact_holdings (read by the holdings-performance producer with the CUSIP, Symbol, Asset Name chain), fact_unrealized (open positions). Lot or event: fact_realized (sold lots). Model, per day: fact_model_roster, fact_model_blend, fact_model_definition, gold dim_model_portfolio. Day: every dated table is one date= partition per date. Household: no household column is named; the relationship keys Relationship ID and Relationship Name (on several silver tables, by name) are the nearest household-like grain and were not measured. Bronze and meta: no grain, raw landings and status markers.
basis_words: Measured in this run: a LIST of blackdiamond/cottonwood/ (four common prefixes, no direct objects), a LIST of each layer, the date= partition count and newest date of every table, and the sorted column names of the first Parquet object in each newest partition, read from its footer only (ranged GET of the tail through pyarrow read_schema). Reads by the worker's own private script: 83 LIST pages, 15 HEAD, 15 ranged footer GETs, and 15 LIST pages of a single-page peek at the zero-partition folders: 128 S3 reads in total and no write. The checker's own reads are not in that count. Not read: no row data in any table; the raw Excel workbooks and JSON files under bronze/ and meta/ (their contents could hold a return column that silver dropped, so a return series there is not ruled out); the c1 and c2 columns of the five _s2 twin tables; every date partition other than the newest footer of each table. Grain words come from column names and the repo reader code named beside them; none was measured on rows. The verdict is the author's judgment under the four definitions in the order, not a computed result.
